Tablet UET 5 81 BM 131236 letter from Nanni to Ea-nasir famous complaint copper. I know published translation but need derive supplied. Famous: "Speak to Ea-nasir: thus says Nanni. Now when you came, you spoke thus to me: 'I will give good copper ingots to Gimil-Sin.' You came and spoke to me thus, but you did not do so. You put bad copper ingots before my messenger and said, 'If you want to take them, take them; if you do not want to take them, go away!' What do you take me for, that you treat me with such contempt? ... I have sent gentlemen like ourselves to collect my money, but you sent me back empty-handed, and that through enemy territory. Is there anyone among the traders who deal with Telmun who has treated me so? You alone treat my messenger with contempt! On account of that copper which you have caused me to remove from my hand, you speak thus. I myself have given to the palace 18 talents of copper, and Sumi-abum has given 18 talents of copper. Apart from what we both have written on the sealed document for the temple of Shamash, how have you treated me for that copper? You have withheld my money through enemy territory; you are obligated to return my money to me in full. Know that I shall not accept here copper that is not of good quality. I shall select and take the ingots in my own yard..." left: "And for the one for whom you have sent me ...? exercise your right of rejection" Need careful line translation.

I need not paraphrase existing. I'll analyze linguistic each.

I'll recall exact common translation of complaint: full:
"Tell Ea-nasir: Nanni sends the following message:
When you came, you said to me as follows: 'I will give Gimil-Sin (when he comes) fine quality copper ingots.' You left then but you did not do what you promised me. You put ingots which were not good before my messenger (Sit-Sin) and said: 'If you want to take them, take them; if you do not want to take them, go away!'
What do you take me for, that you treat somebody like me with such contempt? I have sent as messengers gentlemen like ourselves to collect the bag with my money (deposited with you) but you have treated me with contempt by sending them back to me empty-handed several times, and that through enemy territory. Is there anyone among the merchants who trade with Telmun who has treated me in this way? You alone treat my messenger with contempt! On account of that one trifling talent of copper which you had caused me to remove, you have made me feel such contempt, while I myself have given on your behalf 18 talents of copper to the palace, and Sumi-abum has given 18 talents of copper, apart from what we both have had written on a sealed tablet to be kept in the temple of Shamash.
How have you treated me for that copper? You have withheld my money bag through enemy territory; it is now up to you to restore (my money) to me in full.
Take cognizance that (from now on) I will not accept here any copper from you that is not of fine quality. I shall (from now on) select and take the ingots individually in my own yard, and I shall exercise against you my right of rejection because you have treated me with contempt."
Final: "u3 a-na sza tu-me-i-sza-an-ni na-si-ih-ta-am e-pu-usz-ka" = "and because you have treated me with contempt, I shall exercise against you my right of rejection." nāsiḫtam epēšum = "exercise the right of refusal" perhaps. obverse
To Ea-nasir, speak. Thus says Nanni:

Now, when you came, you spoke to me as follows: "I will give good copper ingots to Gimil-Sin." You came and spoke to me thus, but you did not do it. You placed copper ingots that were not good before my messenger and said: "If you wish to take them, take them; if you do not wish to take them, go away!"

As for me, what do you take me for, […] that you treat me with such contempt? I sent to you men, people like yourself, to collect my money, but you sent them back to me empty-handed, one at a time and two at a time, through enemy territory.
